#2160. Spurs included one Ash Phillips clause that Middlesbrough won’t stop thinking about

Middlesbrough are looking to end a 10-year exile from the Premier League at the end of this season, and are certainly well-placed to do so based on their early-campaign form.

Kim Hellberg was appointed at the Riverside Stadium 12 months ago, but has completely transformed the outlook of the North East side.

The Swede is now one of the most highly-rated head coaches outside the Premier League, whilst many of his squad on Teesside are in similar boats due to their current ability and exceptionally high potential.

Having fallen short in last season's automatic promotion race before losing May's play-off final to Hull City in crushing circumstances, Hellberg was significantly backed by Steve Gibson in the summer to make the desired changes in order to ensure such feats were a one-off.

As many as 12 new signings were recruited by Boro throughout the summer window, with depth and quality being added in equal measure right throughout their squad.

However, three of said dealings were particularly eye-catching in the form of Radek Vitek, Ash Phillips and Will Lankshear, with the latter duo both arriving in big-money moves from Tottenham Hotspur.

Spurs sold Will Lankshear to Boro in the summer, but, they have clauses written into the contract to protect their position in the future.

Phillips is no stranger to the Championship despite being just 21 years of age, having risen through the academy ranks at Blackburn Rovers before featuring 14 times for the Ewood Park outfit.

Spurs then activated a £2m release clause three summers ago, but the centre-back was swiftly loaned to Plymouth Argyle for the second period of 2023/24, with the Devon side narrowly avoiding relegation to League One.

Phillips then spent the past two seasons on loan at Stoke City, racking up 83 appearances in North Staffordshire, with his form and situation in North London subsequently attracting Middlesbrough's attention, whilst the Potters also sought a permanent move.

However, after a long-standing summer saga, during which talks were 'advanced' before hitting the buffers, the Salford native penned a five-year contract at the Riverside Stadium on August 15th.

Despite being so highly-rated, Phillips never made a senior appearance for the North London club, albeit the managerial shake-up which followed his arrival is likely to have contributed to such factors.

Roberto De Zerbi opted to cash in on the England youth international, who would otherwise be competing against the likes of Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Micky van de Ven for a starting berth.

That said, Middlesbrough will certainly be wary of the fact Spurs still stand a chance of making their own significant funds if Phillips reaches his expected potential.

The aforementioned £7m initial deal is followed up by £13m in add-ons, meaning Spurs could make as much as £20m regardless, whilst also inserting a 20 percent sell-on clause within the agreement.

Spurs also have matching rights inserted into the deal, allowing them the potential to reunite with Phillips, irrespective of the fee another club puts on Middlesbrough's desk.

It remains to be seen what the future holds for Phillips, who has already become a mainstay in Hellberg's new-look defence as Middlesbrough set their sights on promotion.

The defender, no doubt, will eventually hope to make his mark in the Premier League too, and the Boro bosses' recent verdict only backs up why Spurs looked to protect themselves during negotiations.

"The thing for him is, and that's why I think he's here, because the way we play challenges him to do the things he needs to do to become a Premier League centre-back.

"I don’t think he is at the moment, but I think in some aspects of the game, he's up with the top, top, top level," he added.

#2159. One lesson Senne Lammens learned after Tottenham’s late equaliser

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Senne Lammens believes Manchester United must learn to finish games off after their late collapse against Tottenham Hotspur.

The result left the goalkeeper frustrated at Old Trafford despite leading the game and with a player more on the field.

Manchester United looked set for three points after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half, but Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory.

Speaking to MUTV, Senne Lammens admitted the team had struggled early on but had done enough after the break to put themselves in a winning position.

“Football can be a bit cruel at times,” the Belgian goalkeeper said. “There are a lot of ups and downs, especially in a game like that.”

Senne Lammens felt United failed to take advantage of Tottenham’s red card, allowing the visitors too much space to find a late equaliser.

“We’ve won a lot of games against 10 men [in the past], but you also know there can be a tricky situation when you’re playing against 10 men, because they have nothing to lose and they know that.”

He added that United should have scored again to put the result beyond doubt or, at the very least, prevented Tottenham from creating further chances.

“I think that’s what we did wrong. We gave them a little bit too much breathing room to create those chances, and then one ball has to go right for them, one bounce has to go their way, and they can score like that.”

The goalkeeper also pointed to similarities with United’s earlier disappointment against Everton, where points slipped away late in the match.

“You feel like those games just slip away from you, and there are one or two situations where you don’t really have control,” he said.

“I think there’s a lot to learn from today. It wasn’t all negative, not at all, but especially the way it ended left a very bad feeling.”

“I think the easy answer is that we have to be able to kill the game faster and not put ourselves in that position to give them a chance.”

Despite the frustration, Lammens said there were positives to take from the performance. However, the late goal had left a bitter feeling, and United now need to turn those lessons into better results.

#2156. Manchester United defence: Why Carrick must trust Yoro and Heaven

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United endured another embarrassing draw against 10-man Tottenham after failing to register their second win despite bringing in a plethora of players.

Manchester United invested heavily last season in their attacking options, bringing in Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

This season, they overhauled their midfield. United spent massively on Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite spending massively, they have failed to produce the control they would have expected in the midfield. The lack of control was evident in the recent Tottenham game, where Mainoo-Tielemans partnership failed to control the game collectively.

The midfield question was covered in our recent report as well, highlighting a lack of control and carried comments from Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp.

The bigger question is when United will strengthen their defence. As per our previous report as well, Manchester United are planning to overhaul their defence in the upcoming transfer windows.

United were heavily linked with several left backs but eventually failed to bring any one. The situation left Luke Shaw as the only senior option in the position, while Patrick Dorgu is used upfront by Michael Carrick.

Harry Amass is another option for Michael Carrick, but he is only here because of a failed transfer move. He has been rarely used at left back as Dalot and Mazraoui get the nod in the position ahead of him.

The situation at right-back isn’t all good either. Diogo Dalot is the first option there, but he rarely provides the assurance that puts Michael Carrick at ease. Noussair Mazraoui is the second choice at right-back, but his attacking numbers aren’t great either.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez form up United’s centre-back pairing while Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven are used all over the defensive line in rotation when needed. Yoro was used at right-back against Tottenham while Heaven arrived as left-back towards the end of the game.

Manchester United’s season hasn’t been defensively strong or anywhere near being good. They have conceded goals in all Premier League games and only kept one clean sheet against Sabah in the Champions League.

Lisandro Martinez has come under scrutiny after errors on four occasions. Against Ipswich Town, Manchester United won 5-2, but his error resulted in Ipswich’s second goal.

His own goal against Fulham gave away two points at Craven Cottage in the 1-1 draw. Another error led to Solanke’s goal against Tottenham, when he took his eyes off the ball.

His injury concerns are another aspect, and maybe Michael Carrick needs to make a decision.

Manchester United’s success depended heavily on youth over the years. When pundits questioned them, Sir Alex Ferguson gave them the chance to prove them wrong. Alan Hansen made the famous quote “You can’t win anything with kids” on the BBC’s Match of the Day on August 19, 1995. United did exactly that, played youth and went on to win everything.

Michael Carrick needs to do exactly that. He needs to trust youth and allow them to make mistakes. Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven arrived as massive potentials, but they haven’t been given the license to express themselves, without fearing for their places. Both the youngsters have rarely started together or in a stretch of games. It is maybe time for them to take their chances.

Michael Carrick needs to keep Harry Maguire as a senior experienced figure around them. There is no doubt over Martinez’s ability, but he is not the answer to United’s long-term problem. United need to blend youth with experience as their identity moving forward. Lisandro Martinez perhaps isn’t the answer to United’s problem.

A defensive revival expected in the upcoming transfer windows needs to happen now. It must happen with chances to the Youth. Michael Carrick needs to be brave enough and throw the youngsters in the mix. What it will bring is a long-term solution. They need to experience the errors and pressures that will shape them in football.

Preston announced the signing today and Docherty told their website: “I’m really proud to be here, to have this badge on my chest and to be part of a club that’s steeped in history. When I told my family, they were all excited and willing me to get it done.

“I’ve always loved playing at Deepdale but haven’t won very often there, so hopefully that will change now. When I was an opposition player, I always found it really difficult. I’ve got family in the north of England and this move just really ticks all the boxes.

Alexander said: “We’re really pleased to bring Greg in. He’s been a captain, won promotions and knows the game inside out.

“Greg’s vocal, fit and motivated, which are all the key things you look for in a professional footballer.

“He has settled into the group really quickly and has a real willingness to show what he can do.”

#2154. Gary Lineker revealed how Sheffield Wednesday icon shaped Spurs decision

Gary Lineker has a Sheffield Wednesday legend to thank for shaping a significant part of his playing career and identity.

The now 65-year-old first came through with Leicester City in the late 1970s before playing for Everton and Barcelona.

The striker came close to breaking the record for goals scored for the England men’s national team, finding the back of the net on 48 occasions from 80 caps.

And in 1989, he returned to English football with a move to Tottenham Hotspur, and he credited a surprising figure for the decision to sign for the London outfit.

Speaking on the Match of the Day Top 10 podcast in 2021, the former BBC presenter revealed that getting the opportunity to play with Chris Waddle was a major factor in his decision to sign for Spurs.

However, he claimed that it was only after he’d agreed to the deal that his agent informed him that the former Sheffield Wednesday star had already signed for Marseille in a big-money move.

“He didn't look like a footballer, but I loved playing with him,” said Lineker, via the BBC.

Ali Al-Hamadi has reflected on his start to life at Sheffield Wednesday on social media, with his team-mate Barry Bannan reacting to the post.

“He was one of the main reasons I signed for Spurs when I left Barcelona.

“I did the deal and I was on holiday in the Caribbean and I got a phone call from my agent saying that he'd been sold to Marseille for £15 million.

“It was like someone just snatching 15 goals a season out of my pocket.

“But he is loved in Marseille, he's a proper cult hero there, he's one of their most popular players in their history.

“And he was the only person who could share a room with Gazza!”

Lineker still went through with the move to White Hart Lane, where he spent three years before departing English football again for a move to Japan with Nagoya Grampus.

During his time with Spurs, the forward scored 67 times from 105 appearances, winning the FA Cup in the process.

Lineker cited Waddle as a major inspiration for his decision to sign for Spurs, but perhaps it would’ve gone differently had he known about his move to Marseille.

The 65-year-old revealed in 2015 that he also had the option to join Manchester United in 1989, who were then managed by Alex Ferguson.

The Scot wanted to partner Lineker with Mark Hughes, with the club targeting a first league title since 1967.

Of course, the Red Devils went on to become a juggernaut in the 1990s, and the former England star must wonder what could’ve been had it not been for Waddle.

It was only after his time at Marseille that Waddle cemented himself as an icon at Sheffield Wednesday.

After three years in France, the playmaker made the switch to Hillsborough ahead of the first ever Premier League season in 1992.

How good was Chris Waddle for Sheffield Wednesday? Comment your opinion below

The now 65-year-old spent four seasons with the Owls, where he made 109 league appearances, contributing 10 goals and 22 assists, with the club finishing seventh, seventh, 13th and 15th in the table.

Even by the standards of someone in the latter stages of his career, Waddle’s performances for the Yorkshire outfit remained quite impressive, and he had a strong final year at Hillsborough, scoring two and assisting six in the Premier League at the age of 34.

While Lineker was unable to enjoy a spell at Spurs with Waddle as his teammate, the pair did, of course, feature together at international level.

In particular, the 1990 World Cup in Italy was a highlight of their time together, with the former Sheffield Wednesday player enjoying a strong tournament that ultimately ended up in disappointment in the penalty shootout in the semi-finals.

That tournament especially highlighted to Spurs fans what could’ve been with Lineker and Waddle working together, as it was England’s best ever showing in the competition on foreign soil until this year’s edition in North America.

#2148. Willian admits Chelsea exit was a ‘big mistake’ after wanting Arsenal escape just THREE months later

Graduate Sports Journalist with a love for football.

Willian has described leaving Chelsea for Arsenal as a mistake, explaining how quickly his enthusiasm for the move turned into regret.

Speaking to former team-mate John Obi Mikel on The Obi One Podcast, the Brazilian revisited the decision that ended his seven-year Stamford Bridge spell in 2020.

Chelsea offered two more years, while Willian wanted three. His contract-length disagreement with Chelsea featured in ReadChelsea’s coverage at the time.

Arsenal offered the longer deal. Willian also valued keeping his family in London and says Mikel Arteta outlined a central role for him.

“To be honest I should have stayed,” he said, in comments reported by the Mirror.

The winger followed the same route as Petr Cech, who explained his own Chelsea-to-Arsenal move through the desire for regular football.

Willian says the reality differed from the picture presented during talks. Within three months, he had told his agent he wanted to leave.

He linked that frustration to his performances, explaining that unhappiness prevented him from producing his best football.

His Arsenal spell ultimately lasted one season. He scored once in 37 appearances before leaving for Corinthians in 2021.

#2147. Why must Manchester United move beyond the Glazers?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Glazers took control of Manchester United in 2005. That takeover has since caused so many disruptions and protests by the fans over massive debts and insufficient backing of the team in the transfer market, despite successful periods in the Premier League and Europe.

Now Manchester United need to think about who should control the club in the future. Laurie Whitwell has now shared his views on why Manchester United need an ownership change. He simply wants the Glazers gone from Old Trafford. However, he also recognizes that replacing the current ownership doesn’t automatically mean things will improve for United.

The journalist believes the change in ownership has had a lasting effect on United, with the club still feeling its consequences today. A fresh start might be welcome, but the identity of the next owners would matter just as much as the departure of the existing ones.

“Personally, I would like to see the Glazers gone from Manchester United,” Laurie Whitwell said on The Rest is Football podcast with Gary Lineker.

“That change, you know, just really affected and still impacts United now.”

The desire for different ownership is one thing, but finding people capable of taking the club forward is another.

Whitwell admitted there is no perfect answer when it comes to who should take charge.

That leaves United facing a difficult choice. A sale could offer the chance to change how the club is run, but simply bringing in a new owner would not guarantee better decisions or a brighter future.

Whitwell also raised the idea of United supporters having a greater say in the club’s ownership and decisions, much like the Barcelona model where fans own the club itself. However, he highlighted that the Barcelona model isn’t ideal either and has its own shortcomings.

Changing the names at the top would only be one part of the change. The club would also need an ownership structure capable of making sound decisions and providing a direction.

The issue of ownership goes beyond whether the Glazers should stay or leave. Manchester United needs to find the right people and the right model to secure the club’s future. Getting that decision wrong could leave them facing the same circus the fans are enduring under the Glazers.

#2146. Burnley must sanction emotional Newcastle switch to fix key problem area

Burnley have endured a nightmare beginning to the 2026/27 Championship campaign following relegation from the Premier League, as the January transfer window looks increasingly important for the Clarets to get right in each passing week.

Burnley were relegated with a whimper from the Premier League last season, but heading back into the Championship, Clarets fans would have naturally been optimistic about their chances, having been automatically promoted the three previous times they found themselves in the division.

However, finding a replacement for Scott Parker proved to be difficult, and in truth, drawn out for way too long, as Belgian head coach Nicky Hayen was handed a poison chalice upon his arrival at Turf Moor.

Hayen won just one of his 12 league games in charge in Lancashire, as well as being knocked out of the League Cup at the hands of League One Bradford City, as incoming Swiss boss Fabio Celestini will be hoping to be given until January to make some much-needed changes to Burnley ranks.

Following his swift appointment, Celestini will have had time to work with his squad in training and identify key areas of improvement, which, in the Clarets’ case right now, is all over the pitch.

However, some positions are more problematic than others, as the options between the sticks right now at Turf Moor aren’t wholly convincing.

Max Weiss started the campaign between the sticks, but after a few high-profile errors, the German was dropped in favour of French goalkeeper Gregoire Coudert, who joined from Brest in the summer.

Since replacing Weiss between the sticks, Coudert has not covered himself in much glory either, shipping four away to Lincoln City and being at fault for Queen’s Park Rangers’ equaliser in their 1-1 draw at Loftus Road, as a highly recognisable name ought to be a priority this January to fix this evident issue.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top 25 most demanding fanbases in British football right now

If the tide doesn’t turn at Burnley sooner rather than later, the Clarets are at risk of following in the footsteps of the likes of Sunderland, Luton Town, and Leicester City to suffer double relegations from the Premier League to League One in consecutive years.

A solid pair of hands between the sticks can be a game-changer, as Celestini must look to bring out-of-favour Newcastle United shot-stopper Nick Pope back to the club in January.

Pope, 34, worked his way up the Football League with the likes of Bury Town, Harrow Borough, Welling United, Charlton Athletic, Cambridge United, Aldershot Town, York City, and Bury before earning a move to Burnley in the summer of 2016, initially acting as deputy to Tom Heaton under Sean Dyche.

155 appearances across all competitions later, Pope had announced himself as one of the finest shot-stoppers in the country, earning ten caps for England during Jordan Pickford’s dominant era, and eventually joining Newcastle United in the summer of 2022 for around £10 million following Burnley’s relegation.

At 34, Pope found himself battling with Southampton outcast Aaron Ramsdale for the number one spot at St James’ Park last season under Eddie Howe, and now is firmly behind Lukáš Horníček in the pecking order.

With Ewen Jaouen and Mark Gillespie also vying for minutes under Mathias Jaissle, Pope’s Newcastle career appears to be coming to a quiet end, as the former England international ought to push for a return to Turf Moor this winter.

Despite his age, few can deny his outstanding shot-stopping ability, and right now, you’d surely do well to find a Burnley supporter who doesn’t believe Pope would walk straight into their side right now in the Championship.

Burnley need a hero, and someone to increase the mood around the place, and given Pope’s situation at Newcastle, he could be the perfect fit.

The only obvious stumbling block is likely his wages, which may be too steep for the Clarets to match, though they would be remiss not to try, as Celestini has one obvious goal heading into January.

Do you think Burnley should look to re-sign Nick Pope from Newcastle in January, or should they be looking elsewhere? Share your thoughts below!

Burnley are in desperate need of an uptick in form sooner rather than later; otherwise, they risk being cut adrift from the rest of the pack.

The January window will provide Celestini with the chance to make some much-needed changes to his squad, and it would be a surprise if a new goalkeeper wasn’t high on his list.

The upcoming window could be Burnley’s last roll of the dice to secure survival, as the Clarets cannot afford to let it pass them by.

Saturday’s Championship tie is the first league meeting of these two sides in fifteen years: The two sides have enjoyed very different histories since the 1 – 1 draw at Ewood Park in 2010. #2143. Fabrizio Romano shares latest on Martinez contract after explosive rant

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Argentinian defender has also apologized to the United higher ups as well over his comments, as shared by Fabrizio Romano.

Lisandro Martinez has held discussions with Jason Wilcox and Michael Carrick after speaking out following United’s 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Martinez had questioned whether Carrick was backed enough in the summer and suggested the club needed changes.

Fabrizio Romano has now confirmed that United consider the matter resolved for now and expect Martinez to remain available for selection.

Speaking about the situation on his YouTube channel, as quoted by Football 365, Romano explained why Martinez’s comments caused concern inside the club.

“He spoke very strongly after the game against Atletico Madrid, which Man Utd lost. It was a very negative moment for the Red Devils. We know that Licha was very strong in his comments. He said that Michael Carrick was not backed enough during the summer transfer window.”

Romano added that Martinez had spoken directly to those at the club after the incident.

“Licha apologised to Man Utd as a club. He spoke to the directors, he spoke to Jason Wilcox, and he spoke to Michael Carrick, who was also involved in this conversation.”

“So, the underlying message remains the same. Lisandro is apologising for the way he expressed himself after a game during a difficult moment for Man Utd, but there was a discussion about the substance of what he said.”

Romano also revealed that United had imposed a financial penalty on the centre-back. However, the punishment does not appear to involve removing him from the squad.

“According to the information available tonight, Lisandro Martinez has been fined.”

He added that Martinez is expected to return to the squad as normal, with the fine considered sufficient punishment for the incident.

“The internal discussion also helped to resolve all the issues. For Man Utd, the case is closed.”

That should bring some immediate clarity to the situation, although questions remain about how the episode could affect Martinez’s longer-term position at Old Trafford.

Romano also pointed towards Martinez’s contract, which expires next summer, with United holding an option to extend it.

“So, let’s see what is going to happen there. For sure, this is the kind of situation that will have an impact on the situation surrounding Lisandro, but we have to see what happens next in terms of future transfers and everything else.”

Chelsea’s official player profile records two league appearances this season, both as a substitute.

In comments reported by Portuguese news agency Lusa, translated from Portuguese, he said:

“Those are the manager’s decisions. I just have to keep giving my best.”

Quenda also acknowledged the quality of his Chelsea team-mates as he attempts to secure more regular football.

The winger joined Chelsea’s early pre-season preparations under Alonso after two seasons in Sporting’s first team. His Chelsea contract runs until 2034.

Quenda is with Portugal Under-21s for Tuesday’s meeting with Czechia, with qualification for next summer’s European Championship already secured.

Chelsea then resume their campaign with Bournemouth’s visit on Saturday 10 October.

For Quenda, the immediate target is straightforward: turn substitute appearances into a first Premier League start. That selection decision remains with Alonso.

Another Saturday afternoon kick-off beckons in this crazy Championship season which offers ‘feast or famine’ football. The second international break kicks in after todays game, with a further maddening two week hiatus after the Hammers’ latest three games in eight days physical assault course.

Surprisingly, only Kyle Walker Peters appears on the ‘injury list’ for West Ham, despite 14 league and 3 cup games already undertaken. Compared with our opponents today who have several players likely out injured, West Ham’s mixture of good luck and good player management seems to be doing the trick again this season, as it did last.

Walker Peters is likely to be the sole enforced absentee in Scott Parker’s match day squad

Speaking ahead of the game, Blackburn Rovers’ veteran coach Tony Mowbray evidently plans to reprise the tactics deployed by Millwall, Southampton, Cardiff and others -and expose West Ham’s well known early defensive frailties:

“”They’re beatable. They’ve lost their manager because they’ve lost too many games this year already and I haven’t seen a team that I think, ‘wow, they’re miles too good for us’.

“Swansea might give that impression, but I think we should be positive, aggressive, play on the front foot and try our hand and see how we get on against West Ham United.” (lancashiretelegraph.co.uk)

West Ham fans will hope to see a more confident, solid foundation created in just a few days – more than Nuno managed to instil in over a year: A tough ask, which is why it may still be far too soon to expect wholesale change.

Scoring the first goal – or two – would prove something of a welcome relief to the 7000 expected Irons fans travelling to the game today, who will all be aware of the Hammers’ terrible propensity to concede first.

As will Parker. Let’s see if he’s managed to instil, at the very least a new combative spirit in his players, and continue on with Wednesday’s second half mentality. Because the Hammers cannot rely on coming back from the dead every week.

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Leeds United welcome Manchester United to Elland Road on Sunday, with both sides looking to put a difficult run of results behind them and get their Premier League season on track.

Leeds United suffered a 2-1 defeat away to Arsenal last weekend despite James Justin scoring to put them in front in the 55th minute.

Manchester United also dropped points in the Premier League, drawing 1-1 with Tottenham, before losing 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League away from home.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to find consistency in recent weeks and have come under immense pressure to get in results. The Whites meanwhile will hope that home advantage can make the difference when United face their bitter rivals on Elland Road.

Leeds have recorded one win, two draws and two defeats in their last five matches in all competitions. Their best result came against Newcastle, where they won, but a 6-3 defeat to Chelsea in the Carabao Cup and the loss to Arsenal have left them searching for a response.

Manchester United have also won just once in their last five matches. Their 4-0 Champions League victory over Sabah FK was the only comfortable win, but defeats to Manchester City and Atletico Madrid, alongside draws against Fulham and Tottenham, have raised questions about their form and Michael Carrick.

Leeds are waiting on Dan James, who returned from international duty with a back problem and missed the Arsenal game. Joe Rodon remains sidelined with a hamstring injury and is not expected back in full training until next month. Harry Wilson could return after being an unused substitute last weekend. Mateo Joseph is also among Leeds’ absentees.

Manchester United have their own concerns. Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo are doubts after picking up issues against Tottenham and missing Tuesday’s trip to Madrid. Benjamin Sesko remains unavailable with a recurring shin problem, while Patrick Dorgu is expected to be out until late November. Manuel Ugarte is recovering from knee surgery, and Noussair Mazraoui is a doubt with a back problem.

There is better news regarding Matthijs de Ligt, who could return to contention. Leny Yoro is also available for selection despite his Champions League suspension.

The match takes place at Elland Road on Sunday, October 18. Kick-off is scheduled for 2 pm BST (1pm GMT).

#2135. West Ham winger has to prove the Tottenham doubters wrong – here’s how

West Ham United and Tottenham Hotspur seem to be holding their noses and doing transfer business with each other after a feud between the two club chairmen prohibited any sort of contact in well over a decade. Now that both Levy and Sullivan have departed, the two seem prepared to trade players once again.

The two sets of fans, of course, revel in player misfortune once transfers have taken place – how West Ham supporters enjoyed Mohammed Kudus’ first season travails and then merely taking £85 million from the Spuds for the signature of Mateus Fernandes and doubling our money seemed sufficient cause for satisfaction.

Quietly banking about £20 million more than the young Portuguese would generate from any other club and heading off financial armageddon with north London money seemed a deal well done.

Spurs fans now have their moment, with the gloating evident over Manor Solomon‘s failure to launch in east London. The winger has struggled despite frequent starting slots under Nuno and must now be facing competition from young Edvin Austbø who has impressed each time he’s stepped onto the turf.

As Tottenham fan site Hotspurhq.com puts it:

“West Ham are saddled with Manor Solomon, who has scored just 2 goals with 2 assists in 14 appearances. The big problem with Solomon that Tottenham have been well aware of is that he is not a team player.

Spurs had to listen to a lot of complaining from him about his minutes or about mistreatment from the club, but the real reason why he didn’t play was because he never showed he was good enough.”

Solomon – there’s a man of the match in there lurking – but many doubt he can he return to that form once again

Identifying the problem as being specifically to do with his mindset rather than his ability, the criticism goes on:

“A big part of that is Solomon does not help his teams win. He holds the ball too much and plays like someone more focused on scoring or piling up his own stats than playing with the team.”

Early on this season, after his man of the match award, there was a feeling that we’d stolen Solomon for a very modest £4 million up – front: Depending on what a decent coaching regime can coax out of the Israeli, there may still be room for quiet satisfaction.

He has the record and the ability, but needs to find a way to return to his best form. When in a Leeds eleven, he looked a top quality prospect indeed and along with Joel Piroe scored 29 times, playing no small part in taking the club back to the Premier League.

Much like his new manager, he’s done it before and knows what is needed. The jury is out as to whether he’s still got it.

#2133. Parker’s past threatens to haunt him over “dire football’ warning | West Ham News

Ask any West Ham fan after last weekend’s 3-1 home loss to West Bromwich Albion whether they’d settle for winning ways at all costs and most would have instantly nodded their agreement.

The second three goal loss at home within eight days had caused the boos to ring out as Nuno’s West Ham train derailed spectacularly, in what was to prove his last game and his ultimate undoing.

Right now there’s a relief flooding around the club as a former hero has returned to take over from negative Nuno. Long may it continue.

However the suggestions are that Parker may not prove to be the all-conquering hero that West Ham seek, judging from his impact at previous clubs. Yes, he knows how to get out of this division and yes, he sure can fix a porous defence – Burnley’s statistics speak for that.

But according to footballleagueworld.co.uk’s article this morning, his time at Burnley divided supporters with his grim, gritty style of play offering little in the way of entertainment:

“The football’s dire. He will bore you to death, and he will cause a fanbase to turn through little snide little comments. He will cause the West Ham fanbase to turn on it.

And that has happened at every single club consistently.”

Few will complain if Scott Parker gets West Ham promoted

Writes their Burnley fan columnist Aaron Wright, condemning Parker’s management style – not results – in the strongest possible terms.

“This is the biggest job he could get, if he can’t get them promoted slash win the league, and if he can’t then keep them in the Premier League, he needs to rethink pretty much everything. He is never getting a bigger job than this and his reputation as a player has helped him get this one. It’s the most guaranteed promotion you will ever have.

“The West Ham fans won’t enjoy it, but I think there’ll be a good respect to it if it turns out how Burnley’s did. 33 games unbeaten is something else.”

Which will have to be a price worth paying, simply to climb back out of this league after the mess of last season and save West Ham from the financial armageddon that not getting promoted would surely deliver.

To paraphrase Jacob Steiberg, Guardian journalist, on Parker’s football shortcomings not succeeding in the Premier League: worry about that next season – first you have to make it back.

#2132. Chelsea sweat on key stars as Bournemouth test looms

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Chelsea return to Premier League action this weekend with a growing treatment table and a lot of questions for Xabi Alonso to answer before Saturday’s visit of Bournemouth.

The main concern revolves around Joao Pedro. Chelsea’s current player of the season rescued a point against newly promoted Hull, but he suffered a knock and sat out the damaging 3-0 defeat at Brentford. The problem also prompted his removal from Brazil’s squad shortly after he had returned to it.

It is understood that he is undergoing specialist knee treatment in an attempt to expedite his recovery, although reports in Brazil suggest that he could be out for up to four weeks. No date has yet been set, but a return later in October looks most likely.

There is more good news elsewhere. Cole Palmer was among the players called up to the latest England squad, which did not go down too well with Thomas Tuchel.

The midfielder has been recovering from a persistent groin injury and has been working with a rehab coach. He is likely to be fit this weekend.

Moises Caicedo has also struggled with an injury this season, playing just 14 minutes across the campaign. He’s spent the majority of time on the bench recovering from a bad calf injury, which ruled him out for most of the season.

He made his only appearance as a substitute against his former club Brighton, but the game was red-flagged for Ecuador’s friendlies, so he did not play.

Alonso said before the Brentford match that the player would be ready to return. It seems to be the case, unless something went wrong.

Captain Reece James missed the Brentford game with yet another hamstring problem. Alonso said he only just missed out, so a return seems likely.

There may also be debuts. Marco Palestra, the £27m signing from Atalanta, has been sidelined since a training injury just before the opening match against Fulham. He is back in full training and was expected to feature in a behind-closed-doors friendly with Portsmouth. Chelsea lost 2-0. Emmanuel Emegha, injured after scoring against Bromley in July, is also pushing for involvement.

Less clear is the position of Jamie Gittens. He limped off with an ankle injury playing for England Under-21s against Kazakhstan and was seen on crutches. Mike Penders is fine after a quad scare on Belgium duty. Returning to the bench against Turkey.

Chelsea badly need a lift. Defeat at Brentford before the break left Alonso’s side looking shaky, and a squad stretched by injuries has not helped.

Saturday brings a chance to steady things. If Palmer, James and Caicedo are available, with Palestra and Emegha potentially adding fresh options, the picture will look much brighter at Stamford Bridge. Joao Pedro’s absence will still sting. However, a strong response against Bournemouth would go a long way towards easing the pressure and restoring belief.

#2131. Arsenal transfer news: Bournemouth make Eli Junior Kroupi decision ahead of January window

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have been dealt a potential setback in their pursuit of Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi. The Cherries are reportedly refusing to consider a January sale.

The Gunners are not alone in keeping an eye on the 20-year-old after he returned from injury. Manchester United have also made enquiries, and Tottenham remains a strong possibility after chasing him over the summer.

However, Bournemouth are keen to keep Kroupi at the Vitality Stadium following the January transfer window. His return will provide new head coach Marco Rose with another attacking threat. Helping to improve their position in the Premier League.

This could mean that Arsenal will have to plan a long-term pursuit of the player.

Kroupi provided a positive impression in his debut season in English football. Becoming one of the most exciting young forwards in the Premier League.

Overall, he hit the target on 13 occasions in the previous league campaign. Attracting the attention of a number of top European clubs.

Paris Saint Germain, Barcelona, Chelsea and Tottenham were among the clubs that were said to keep following his progress over the summer months.

However, he was unable to make the move after suffering an injury to his foot which required surgery. Kroupi has now returned to action. He came on as a late substitute in Bournemouth’s 3-0 victory against Manchester United last weekend.

Arsenal have again been linked. The Gunners are now known to be one of a number of clubs to have asked about the player’s injury and fitness ahead of improving their attacking options.

Tottenham are also interested, having had previous interest in signing him. There is no real suggestion an offer has been made.

Bournemouth are the main problem for Arsenal, with Kroupa said to be unwilling to leave the Cherries in January. He is seen as an important asset for them in the second half of the season.

However, Rose’s side has had a difficult start to the season so far. Having him at his disposal could prove to be vital. The forward can bring goals and quality into the attack. Bournemouth believes it will help change their fortunes in the coming months.

They will also look to keep their attacking unit intact. Players such as Rayan and Marcus Tavernier are ones that Bournemouth will look to keep hold of. Alex Scott may also catch the eye of other clubs ahead of the New Year.

Bournemouth will be desperate to avoid losing a number of key players in one transfer window.

That stance leaves Arsenal facing a difficult decision if they want to pursue Kroupi. The Gunners can continue monitoring his performances and fitness, but a January move currently looks unlikely.

The forward’s return to regular football will give interested clubs another opportunity to assess his progress. Arsenal, Tottenham and Manchester United could therefore remain attentive to developments as the season continues.

Bournemouth are currently in the best position and Arsenal might have to wait until the summer to see how the Cherries will hold up when faced with losing one of their most promising young players.

#2130. Jamie Carragher names Man Utd Star who impressed him against Leeds

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United had a difficult evening once again as they were held to a 1-1 draw at Leeds United. Pressure mounts on Michael Carrick as United have just 7 points from 7 games.

Manchester United took the lead through Bryan Mbeumo in the first half, with the forward finishing Youri Tielemans’ excellent cross from the right. However, the visitors couldn’t hold on to their advantage as Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised for Leeds United from a corner.

The draw extended United’s frustrating run of results, leaving Michael Carrick still searching for the consistency his side need.

Carragher, though, believes there were positives to take from the trip, particularly one performance at the back.

Jamie Carragher has singled out Harry Maguire for praise after Manchester United drew 1-1 with Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday.

Speaking on Sky Sports, the former Liverpool defender admitted that picking up a point at Elland Road was not necessarily a bad result in isolation, even if United’s recent form made it feel like a missed opportunity.

“Going away to Leeds is going to be tricky for any team except for Manchester City and Arsenal at the moment,” Carragher said.

“A lot of teams will take a point at Leeds this season but the problem for Manchester United is the results have been so poor that they need to start winning games so it almost feels like two points dropped.”

Carragher then turned his attention to Maguire, who he felt played a major role in keeping United in the game when Leeds began to push for a winner.

“But in isolation, getting a point at Leeds is a decent result. I thought Harry Maguire was fantastic, especially in the second half.”

Leeds United grew into the contest after Calvert-Lewin brought them level, putting United under pressure during the closing stages. Carragher felt Maguire’s efforts in defence helped prevent the visitors from falling apart.

“After Leeds got that goal back there was a stage of the game where it felt like Man United could go under, but Maguire at the back held it together for them. He was fantastic.”

The result may feel like another opportunity missed for Carrick, but Maguire’s performance gave United something positive to take away from Elland Road.

#2128. Chelsea co-sporting director Laurence Stewart to leave in leadership reshuffle

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

The departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

The changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not currently planning to recruit a replacement.

#2127. Arsenal could expose Liverpool’s biggest weakness at Anfield

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have spent years struggling to impose themselves at Anfield. However, Mikel Arteta could have an opportunity to change that record when his side face Liverpool on Sunday.

The Gunners have often struggled against the physicality of Liverpool on Merseyside. Since Jurgen Klopp took charge, Liverpool have built a reputation for being high pressing, fast, and making their opponents make mistakes.

However, looking at the latest stats, it seems that Liverpool are no longer as physical, meaning that Arsenal could target their weaknesses.

The disparity is stark between the two teams, with Liverpool having run the least distance of any Premier League side this season. Meanwhile, Arsenal are running the most.

If Arteta’s side can capitalise on this and create fast attacks from possession, then they can utilise this to their advantage.

Liverpool have shifted away from their high-octane style associated with much of Klopp’s reign. Arne Slot has slowly moved towards a more possession-based approach, focusing on keeping the ball.

Andoni Iraola looks keen to add more intensity to their pressing. The Reds have had some of the best pressing stats in the Premier League this season (Opta Analyst).

However, they are not getting the desired intensity from the system.

In addition to chasing the opposition when they have the ball, players must quickly recover, cut off passing lanes and return to their defensive positions.

This is where Arsenal might have an opportunity. If they can get past Liverpool’s first line of pressure, they may have space to push forward before the home side can get back into position.

Another area that the Gunners could target is Liverpool’s midfield.

Alexis MacAllister and Ryan Gravenberch are technically gifted and very composed when they have the ball. But neither are a true defensive midfielder, which raises questions over their ability to stop teams playing through the middle.

Arsenal have the players to exploit this. Declan Rice can put in an energetic, physical performance and drive the play forward. Myles Lewis-Skelly provides another option who can run with the ball into dangerous areas.

This can cause problems for the Liverpool midfield. Arsenal can try to disrupt Mac Allister and Gravenberch, not letting them set the tempo of the game.

If they win these individual battles, it can stop Liverpool from getting the ball control they want.

The task is certainly a tall one. Arsenal have lost their last 16 games at Anfield, including seven in Arteta’s reign.

Whilst that may be the case, the current Liverpool team are very different to the one Arsenal have faced on a regular basis during Klopp’s time in charge.

They certainly can’t expect to be outplayed, but they must take advantage of Liverpool’s failings.

Arsenal are currently second in the Premier League with 21 points from eight games. They will want to win here but will need to do more than just run them into the ground.

If Rice and Lewis-Skelly can push forward and pressurise them, forcing them to make mistakes, then Arteta could finally have his winning recipe at Anfield.

#2126. Como vs Man Utd Preview: Team news, injuries, form and where to watch

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United travel to Italy on Wednesday, looking for their first win since September 10, when they face Como in the Champions League.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to build any momentum this season. Sunday’s 1-1 draw against Leeds extended their winless run to six matches in all competitions, leaving United with just seven points from their opening seven Premier League games.

The pressure on Carrick continues to grow. A win in Europe would offer some relief, but Como will not make life easy for Manchester United.

Manchester United began their Champions League campaign with a convincing 4-0 win over Sabah FK but lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in their next match. They have since drawn with Leeds, having also failed to beat Fulham and Tottenham in the Premier League.

Their last six matches across all competitions have produced three draws and three defeats. Michael Carrick is in pressure of his own and needs a response from his players, particularly with United sitting 13th in the Premier League and 13th in the Champions League standings.

Como have shown more promise. Cesc Fabregas’ side beat RB Leipzig 4-1 in Europe before losing 3-2 to Feyenoord. They returned to winning ways against Fiorentina, claiming a 3-1 victory that moved them up to fifth in Serie A, with 14 points from seven games.

Como have scored 11 goals and conceded eight across their last six matches in all competitions. United have struggled, with their only clean sheet of the season coming against Sabah FK.

United have several confirmed absentees ahead of the trip to Italy. Patrick Dorgu, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko are ruled out, while Leny Yoro is suspended for the European fixture after picking a red against Atletico Madrid.

Lisandro Martinez is a major concern after coming off at half-time against Leeds with a thigh problem. Ayden Heaven, Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo are all doubtful for the game.

Como will be without Assane Diao, who is sidelined with a thigh injury. Moise Kean has a shin problem and is a doubt, while Trevoh Chalobah is also a fitness concern with a muscular issue.

The match takes place at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Wednesday, October 21, with kick-off at 5:45 pm BST.

UK viewers can watch the Champions League fixture live on TNT Sports 2 and HBO Max.

#2125. Veltman’s West Ham Admission Highlights Parker’s First Big Problem

West Ham defender Joël Veltman has admitted that the Hammers’ habit of starting matches poorly must change, with Scott Parker facing an immediate challenge against Blackburn Rovers this afternoon.

Speaking in an interview with the club’s official website, Veltman acknowledged that Wednesday’s disastrous first half against Cardiff City was hardly an isolated incident. West Ham recovered from three goals down to draw 3-3, but the Dutchman knows they cannot keep relying on second-half comebacks.

“It wasn’t the first time we haven’t started so well,” admitted Veltman, who wants West Ham to begin against Blackburn with the same intensity they showed after the interval in Wales.

Personally, I think West Ham’s slow starts and early capitulations are definitely a mentality problem. Nothing demonstrated that more clearly than the transformation at half-time against Cardiff, when a team that had looked completely traumatised and shell-shocked suddenly emerged looking like an entirely different side.

Of course, some of that improvement was tactical, but I’m not entirely convinced how many tactics you can impart in 15 minutes. What Parker, Mark Noble and Jarrod Bowen clearly managed to do was give the players a lift, and the difference in their attitude was extraordinary.

I’ve thought from day one that this was probably the easiest improvement any new manager could make with the current group of players. If West Ham approach matches with a positive attitude and a genuine desire to win rather than playing fearfully, I suspect much of the problem could be addressed with a decent team talk.

That doesn’t mean tactics and team selection are irrelevant, but the players have already demonstrated they possess considerably more ability than their recent performances suggest. Parker’s first job is surely to convince them of that.

Veltman himself was absolutely brilliant during the second half against Cardiff, and I think he could become an important player under Parker. His composure and positioning at right-back could allow Jarrod Bowen the freedom to drift into central areas, where the West Ham captain caused absolute havoc on Wednesday evening.

Bowen was instrumental in the comeback, and having a dependable defender behind him could make that attacking freedom much easier to accommodate. It’s another reason why I’d like to see Veltman retain his place against Blackburn.

The defender certainly recognises the opportunity ahead, telling the club: “We want to go into another away game on Saturday and start where we finished.”

That really is the challenge for Parker. West Ham don’t need to discover some previously hidden ability between now and kick-off; they need to reproduce the confidence, aggression and positive mentality they finally showed during those remarkable 45 minutes against Cardiff.

#2124. Arsenal news: Arsenal vs Liverpool. Arteta targets Anfield record as Liverpool prepare for Premier League clash

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal vs Liverpool: Arsenal travel to Anfield on Sunday looking to maintain their strong start to the Premier League season and end a long wait for victory at Liverpool’s home ground.

A blistering start to the season has seen Mikel Arteta’s side win seven of their first eight league games, leaving them tied on points with Manchester City at the top of the table and six points ahead of Liverpool going into the game.

However, the Gunners have not beaten Liverpool in the Premier League at Anfield since 2012/13. Arteta will be aware that the Reds are starting to gel under Andoni Iraola.

They have won three of their last four league games after a lacklustre start and had their first league win at home this season with their 2-0 win over Brighton.

After replacing Arne Slot over the summer, Iraola brought his impressive three-year spell at Bournemouth to Anfield. However, Liverpool have struggled to adjust to the new manager, losing 3 of their first 4 league games.

But they have recently improved and are looking to play a much faster style of football. As Adrian Clarke notes, they are pressing more, not sitting back as much and wanting to attack quickly when they win the ball.

They have been the most direct attackers in the Premier League. They have pace to spare within their attack, with players like Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo providing a threat in advanced areas.

Isak comes into the game in good form after finding the back of the net six times in his first eight league games. He has scored in three successive games in the Premier League for the first time since joining the club.

Florian Wirtz will also play a key role in Liverpool’s attacking play. The German has been consistently creating chances for the team playing behind Isak in a 4-2-3-1 system. He has created nine chances against Brentford.

Arsenal will need to limit the space available to Liverpool’s forward players. Allowing Isak and Gakpo to combine freely could make an already difficult away fixture even harder.

Arsenal have had some positive news on their squad ahead of their Merseyside trip. Declan Rice and Riccardo Calafiori are both back in training.

Christos Tzolis has also trained after missing October. Noni Madueke has also not been ruled out by Arteta ahead of Sunday’s match after he missed the Fleetwood game.

They also have their own fitness issues to contend with. Iraola confirmed that Dominik Szoboszlai and Victor Munoz are both available after suffering injuries earlier in the month.

Jeramie Frimpong will be missing due to a hamstring issue but should be back after the international break. Hugo Ekitike, Geovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley are all still sidelined with longer-term injuries.

The presence of Rice will be key for Arsenal. He has been one of the best progressive midfielders in the Premier League, along with their captain, Martin Odegaard.

Despite losing just one of their last eight Premier League clashes against Liverpool, Arsenal are not as strong on the road.

The Gunners have not won any league games in their last 13 trips to Anfield. They have drawn five and lost eight. Their last win was a 2-0 victory back in the 2012/13 season.

They have also never gone 14 games unbeaten away from home in the league. That would be a great achievement.

However, there is good reason to believe they can do it. They have only conceded five clean sheets in the league this season. They have faced the least number of shots on target and the fewest expected goals.

Liverpool have also been on a strong run defensively with four clean sheets in their last six league games, so Arsenal must make their chances count.

A win would provide another key result against a direct rival, improving their position at the top of the Premier League table and finally putting an end to one of the clubs’ longest-running away day woes.

#2122. What Martin O'Neill told Kasper Hogh about Celtic goal drought after Besiktas

As German referee Sascha Stegemann sounded his full-time whistle, Martin O'Neill raised his right fist to the smoke-filled Glasgow sky.

Celtic's Europa League campaign was finally up and running courtesy of a frenetic 3-2 victory over Besiktas, the manager visibly relieved and triumphant in equal measure.

O'Neill usually heads straight up the tunnel after matches. Thursday evening was different. He instead made a beeline for his players before their customary walk round on the Celtic Park turf, embracing captain Callum McGregor and goalscorers Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran.

A turning point in Celtic's season? It's too early to say. But O'Neill knew for certain that failure to beat Besiktas would have rendered the remainder of Celtic's Europa League campaign meaningless. Now they have fresh hope and a platform for progress.

O'Neill insists they must build on their gutsy European victory.

"That is what we want to do, absolutely," O'Neill said. "From the European side, we have given ourselves a chance. We will have to go and win away from home and it will not be easy."

Thursday evening saw the manager make five changes to his lineup. Jordan Lotomba recorded his first start at right-back and Kasper Hogh, Sebastian Tounekti, and James Forrest made up a second string frontline.

From Forrest, O'Neill wanted experience and added defensive security. Hogh offered a focal point in attack and went off to a standing ovation in the 77th minute.

It marked his 15th Celtic appearance without a goal but the home crowd were appreciative of his work rate, as was O'Neill.

"I want centre-forwards to be able to hold it and that is what he did," O'Neill stated. "He is not Duran, he is not a dribbler. But if he can do this for us against strong opposition it will stand him in good stead.

"I think Thursday night will be good for him. I said to him that I’m not worried about whether he scores a goal.

"Of course you want centre-forwards to score and of course centre-forwards live on them. But I said to him that last night I wanted him to be strong and fight when the ball is played up to him.

"I thought in terms of holding the ball up and bringing people into the game that he did really well."

Hogh, signed from Bodo/Glimt for a club record transfer fee in excess of £11 million during the summer transfer window, had no opportunities against Besiktas.

The Dane registered just one touch in the opposition penalty area and didn't have a single shot on goal.

Hogh is being starved of the service upon which he thrived at Bodo.

To that concern, O'Neill responded: "If they are going man for man and we have gone really, really low in terms of going close to the goalkeeper then the next one in if you are dinking it in is where a centre-forward has to play.

"If it is a decent ball in then he has to hold it up because he should be first. If it is in the air and he has to fight for it then it is difficult. But if you dink it in for him then you can start from there."

"Centre-forwards need a goal," O'Neill continued. "But that performance there against European opposition will give him confidence. I don’t know what side we will play on Sunday. But this lad has scored goals in the Champions League remember.

"He will get a confidence boost from Thursday night in terms of doing that part of the game well. But it will be nice for him to score a goal."

Hogh needn't have to worry about goals if Duran maintains his apex form. The Colombian couldn't have been more influential after coming off the bench against Besiktas, netting a crucial brace to give Celtic all three points.

First, Duran latched on to Osmand's reverse pass, rounding opposition goalkeeper Alexander Nubel and slotting into an empty net. He then brilliantly controlled Kieran Tierney's wayward shot, this time beating Nubel from six yards out.

"At this minute, he is on fire," O'Neill said of Duran. "He can play wide right, he has done that. He has played wide left for his other club. But centre-forward is where he is dynamic."

When Duran plays through the middle, Hogh is often sacrificed. Conversely, Hogh starting usually sees Duran shifted to the right flank. For O'Neill, it's onerous finding the perfect balance.

"We made five changes on Thursday night because it was necessary," he explained. "The boys who came on were always going to come on after 60 minutes.

"You can’t just plan things like this. Somebody might pick up an injury. Things change during the course of the game. But the plan before it was for these lads to go on. We were always going to make the changes.

"It was necessary if we wanted a bit more gusto in the side and a bit more playing in behind. That gave the opportunity for Duran to weave a bit of magic."

Focus rightly lay on Celtic's attacking play after Thursday. Yet their defence was equally pivotal, limiting Besiktas to few opportunities of note.

Beyond a penalty and the resulting rebound, from which they scored, Vincenzo Italiano's side offered little in the way of forward penetration, struggling to break down Celtic's organised structure. It took a long-range effort from Orkun Kokcu to score their second of the evening.

"It was really pleasing and really important," O'Neill said of his team's defending. "We conceded some ground in the game which was to be expected, but I thought defensively we were really, really strong.

"When corners came in we dealt with them and we dealt with second balls as well after it was played out. The back four was terrific. Lotomba did well until he conceded the penalty."

Central defender Cameron Carter-Vickers had one of his better displays. The American made nine clearances and won all but one of his five duels. Accurate on the ball too, Carter-Vickers brought an air of stability to the backline.

He recovered ably from his performance against Falkirk last weekend, when his meek clearance led directly to Ethan Ross' opener. Carter-Vickers came off in the latter stages with a hamstring complaint, but O'Neill thinks he had a point to prove.

"It looked that way," said the Celtic boss. "I thought he was very strong. He was complaining about his hamstrings being very tight at half-time and I thought we would give him another 15 minutes.

"Of course, the game changed in that time and we were chasing the game from behind. But the lads who came on in the forward positions were always going to come on. James Forrest was never going to last the whole game.

"I thought he was outstanding, an absolute credit to the football club with what he did for us. Even defensively. Everybody worked so hard. It was really pleasing."

The key for Celtic and O'Neill is building on Thursday's thrilling victory. As the manager knows all too well, it'll count for nothing if Kilmarnock, St Mirren, and Torreense aren't beaten in the coming weeks.

#2120. Rio Ferdinand disappointed Man Utd didn’t sign midfielder better than Elliot Anderson

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Rio Ferdinand has admitted he is disappointed that Manchester United failed to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi, with the highly-rated midfielder now making an impression at Manchester City.

Manchester City beat several rivals to secure Bouaddi’s signature over the summer in a deal worth £86 million. The Morocco international became the Premier League’s most expensive teenager, and Rio Ferdinand believes Manchester United missed out on a special talent.

The former United defender was particularly impressed by Bouaddi’s second-half cameo during City’s Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain last week. His performance reminded Rio Ferdinand why he had been talking about the youngster throughout the previous year and during the summer transfer window.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ferdinand highlighted how Bouaddi was the highlight of the game against PSG and who they missed.

“He came on and showed PSG that they may have missed out on someone who was on their doorstep when he was playing in France,” Ferdinand said.

The former England international also confirmed that Manchester United had been interested in bringing the midfielder to Old Trafford, but the transfer fee was too expensive.

“Manchester United were in for him, 100%, but the fee was just too much,” he added.

Ferdinand was left frustrated by what he saw from the teenager, who turned 19 this month.

“Just that little cameo against PSG makes you go, ‘oh, I can’t believe we missed out on that. I can’t believe it.’ I’m so gutted, so gutted. He’s bad! He’s so calm under pressure.”

Rio Ferdinand suggested Bouaddi’s quality could soon make the midfield position in a packed Manchester City his regular role.

City already have Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez among their midfield options, but Ferdinand believes Bouaddi has the ability to stand out alongside them.

“They’ve got Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez in that midfield as well but this kid could be the best of the three, easily.”

#2119. Arsenal injury news: Arteta faces selection dilemma ahead of Liverpool clash

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal will have a few key injury updates ahead of their clash with Liverpool on Sunday, but Mikel Arteta still has some tough choices to make in his front line.

Declan Rice, Riccardo Calafiori and Christos Tzolis have returned to training so there is hope they can play in the Premier League clash against Anfield.

Bukayo Saka is still out with a quad injury, but Noni Madueke looks to be fit to go into the final game. Max Dowman is also suspended after Arsenal were unable to overturn his red card suspension after the defeat to Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup.

However, Arteta has some good options to choose from. He can ill afford any more injuries in attack.

Rice’s return will be key after missing the midweek cup clash.

The midfielder was subbed in the win against Everton with a knock. His absence was a blow against Fleetwood.

He trained on Friday. As long as he does another session on Saturday, he will be available. Rice is a big boost for Arsenal in the middle of the park as they face a Liverpool side who have been in good form recently.

Calafiori is also edging closer to a return. The Italian has played in the last seven Premier League games for Arsenal but missed against Everton.

However, he was only on for a short period when he came on as a sub. But he seemed to have an issue. Arteta said that it didn’t seem like a big problem, but they’re taking some caution.

Like Rice, Calafiori trained on Friday and will be able to go to Merseyside if he finishes his session on Saturday.

Tzolis is another possible addition. The winger has missed Arsenal’s last five matches after suffering a hamstring injury while playing for Greece in October.

His latest scan showed encouraging progress, and he has now returned to training. A further successful session would put him in contention for Sunday’s match.

The main issue for Arteta will be his lack of attacking width.

Madueke did not join the squad for the trip to Fleetwood due to an ankle injury sustained in the Everton game. He did not train on Monday, but Arteta has not ruled him out of the game against Liverpool. He will have to finish his session on Saturday.

Dowman is also missing due to suspension. He was sent off in the 1-1 draw against Fleetwood after a challenge from Harrison Neal. His appeal was rejected by the FA, so he will miss the game against Liverpool.

Saka makes it even worse for the Gunners. The England international has a quad injury from the Bayern Munich game and is likely to be out for several weeks.

Arteta confirmed that he will need another scan before there is a clearer timeline for his return but is likely to be out for a long period of time.

William Saliba is still missing from the squad, having aggravated a back injury during his time playing for France at the World Cup this summer.

But the defender has returned to doing one-on-one training on the training ground.

Arsenal will perform an MRI scan to monitor his progress. Arteta has suggested there have been positive signs, and he is expected back in December.

The main talking point will be Rice, Calafiori and Tzolis returning to training ahead of Sunday.

It would give Arsenal a nice boost with all three players fit. Madueke is still a doubt and they have fewer options going forward with Saka and Dowman out.

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. Bournemouth’s determination to keep Alex Scott has done little to discourage Chelsea, who remain among the leading contenders to sign the England midfielder.

The Blues had a £64m bid rejected during the summer, but their interest has continued into the new season. According to Matt Law of The Telegraph, Chelsea are at the front of the queue of clubs monitoring the 23-year-old.

Bournemouth, however, have no intention of allowing Scott to leave in January. talkSPORT reported this week that the south coast club remain determined to retain him, despite his reluctance to sign a contract extension.

Scott’s current deal runs until 2028, leaving Bournemouth with time to negotiate, although their position could become more complicated if no agreement is reached before next summer.

The midfielder’s immediate priority is recovering from a thigh injury sustained while representing England. He impressed during the 7-0 Nations League victory over Croatia but was withdrawn after 70 minutes. Subsequent examinations revealed a quadriceps problem, with BBC Sport reporting that he could miss six to eight weeks.

His absence is a setback for Bournemouth, who have relied heavily on the former Bristol City midfielder this season. It also introduces another consideration for clubs monitoring his progress ahead of the January window.

Chelsea are not alone in their admiration. Arsenal and Liverpool have also been linked with Scott, whose performances have attracted attention beyond the Premier League.

Suggestions circulating on social media that Bournemouth have already agreed to let him leave in January remain unsubstantiated. There has been no reliable confirmation of such an arrangement, and the club’s reported position is firmly against a winter sale.

For Chelsea, the more realistic opportunity may come next summer, particularly if Scott continues to resist signing a new contract.
