#1965. Scaroni comments on ‘fantastic week’ and Cardinale’s tears: “His passion shows”

AC Milan president Paolo Scaroni believes it has been a ‘fantastic week’ for the club, also commenting on Gerry Cardinale’s passion.

This evening, Milan will host Hungarian giants Ferencvaros at San Siro at 18:45 CET in the fourth game of their Europa League league phase campaign. The Rossoneri hope to build on the derby win and start moving in the right direction in Europe, having lost two of three so far.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Arriving at the customary UEFA lunch, Scaroni was interviewed by the MilanNews correspondent who was present. He spoke about an important past few days, which saw the official unveiling of the new stadium, followed a few hours later by the 3-1 victory in the Milan derby.

First the stadium and then the derby, a fantastic week…

“It’s been a fantastic week. We’re always confident, Gerry Cardinale is too.”

“His passion shows when things are going well and when they are going badly, like everyone else. This time, things went well.”

Milan will have to be at their best tonight, given that their opponents from Budapest have won all three games in Europe thus far, and are 20 unbeaten across all competitions in a run that stretches back to the end of July.

#1964. Champions League RECAP: Man City edge thriller against RB Leipzig and Arsenal hold on for win at Slavia Prague

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER and LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER

Relive Daily Mail Sport's coverage of Wednesday's Champions League fixtures, with Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester City all in action.

The Champions League always manages to deliver.

We started the night with a shock upset as Fenerbahce managed to come from behind twice to defeat Liverpool in Istanbul - and the Reds' fans are not happy about it; there is a meltdown on X.

Then we were treated to a further 39 goals, including Como's record-equalling 9-1 crushing of Lens. I still can't get over that one.

Manchester City and Arsenal both played their parts in the goal-fest, bagging victories for themselves.

Now, we need to shoot off, but thank you once again for joining us on another entertaining night of footie.

We will see you all very soon. Goodnight.

You can watch the full highlights from Arsenal's win by clicking below.

It wasn't classic Arsenal, but they got the job done. And they were good in the first-half, with some good goals from players that needed them.

The Gunners are sitting pretty in third in the table, with three wins and that draw against Bayern Munich.

They will be pretty confident of reaching the last-16 again. Here's what they have left in the league:

Joleon Lescott, former Man City defender, TNT Sports:

I feel like his Man City career has been a bit of an odd one. He was never meant to be No 1, until he became available, and they jumped.

City ended up again selling one of the best young goalkeepers in Europe in James Trafford to accommodate him, and he's not really repaid them. Quite a few errors lately.

And there were loads tonight too. His handling was all over the place - and what even was that positioning for Baku's goal?

Maresca has had to defend him recently. And he's not having the best time of it.

You'd expect City to at least get top 16, but they will really be eyeing up top eight to save that play-off round.

And they have some tough fixtures still to come.

Hard to predict what will happen at the minute.

Slavia Prague and the Champions League are a match made in... hell.

By suffering defeat to Arsenal tonight the Czech side have equalled a rather bad record.

They are now on a 23-game winless run in the Champions League (and European Cup). Both AEK Athens (1989-2006) and FCSB (2006-2013) share that record with Slavia Prague.

Will they ever win a match in this tournament?

David Raya, Arsenal goalkeeper, speaking to TNT Sports:

Mikel Arteta, Arsenal boss, speaking to TNT Sports:

By winning tonight, the Gunners have extended their unbeaten run to 19 games in the Champions League.

Some of you may say, 'well, what about the final defeat to PSG?'. Technically, they drew that game and lost on penalties, so the unbeaten run is intact.

Are PSG the only team better on the planet? I think so.
